newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise despite German WPI surprise.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise despite German WPI surprise.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Friday, with welcome U.S. sales data outweighing dismay at higher than expected German May wholesale prices.
"Thursday's lower than forecast U.S. retail sales figures for May are keeping sentiment up," a dealer said.

At 0720 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.11, yielding 6.16 percent, up from 111.98 on Thursday. The seven percent 2007 bond, which becomes the benchmark on September 1, was up 0.18 point, at 104.73, yielding 6.35 percent.
The crown was virtually unchanged at 3.8068 to the mark.
The 2006 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 45 bp, with the 2007-bund differential also one point down at 65 bp.
The 2006's June future was up 0.59 to 112.09 and the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 rose 0.50 to 90.50. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969650
